deal_summary: A request for label applicators integrated into the customer’s existing conveyor replaced the original full-machine proposal as the main technical question. The customer supplied a production video and the manager forwarded it to production; the retained view ends before a feasibility assessment is recorded (evidence: 1-2,5-6,8-9).

customer_need.summary: The customer wanted applicators added to its existing conveyor rather than a self-contained machine with its own conveyor. A manager worklog records the application as a flat 10-liter HDPE canister with two side labels and about 1,000 units per hour; those numeric/product details are manager-reported (evidence: 0,6).

deal_dynamics.early: A manager worklog describes the initial labeling need; the customer then sent a canister drawing and label dimensions, which the manager routed for technical review (evidence: 0-2).
deal_dynamics.middle: After receiving the proposal, the customer said it had only reviewed it partly and would compare options. It then clarified that only the applicators were needed for the existing conveyor and questioned how the offered self-contained machine could be adapted (evidence: 3-6).
deal_dynamics.late: The customer initially delayed the requested video, then sent production footage; the manager acknowledged receipt and passed it to production. No fit assessment or revised scope is present in the retained view (evidence: 7-9).

positive_signals: The customer supplied a canister sketch and label examples with dimensions (evidence: 1).
The customer clarified the integration requirement and later provided the requested production video (evidence: 6,8).
customer_behavior.initiative: The customer identified that its existing conveyor had to be reused, explained that only applicators were needed, and followed through with production footage (evidence: 6,8).
customer_behavior.decision_process: The customer said it would compare the proposal; whether the revised scope and price were workable depended on a technical review of its existing line and the submitted video (evidence: 5-6,9).

strong_actions: Sent the proposal, asked for the information needed to evaluate integration, and forwarded the customer’s video to production (evidence: 3-4,6,9).
manager_behavior.follow_up_quality: The manager continued follow-up on the video, acknowledged it when received, and routed it for review; a production response is not visible before the view ends (evidence: 7-9).
manager_behavior.next_step_control: The next visible step was a production assessment of the footage, followed by a clear integration scope and any corresponding price revision; neither appears in the retained view (evidence: 6,9).

turning_points.description: The customer clarified that its existing conveyor should be reused and that it needed the applicators rather than the offered self-contained machine; it asked whether this configuration was feasible and would affect price.
The customer sent production footage, and the manager confirmed that it had been passed to production for review.

primary_trajectory_explanation.explanation: The retained trajectory turns on a scope and compatibility question: the customer needed applicators integrated with its existing conveyor, while the proposal described a self-contained machine. The customer supplied footage and the manager routed it for production review, but the retained view ends before that review is answered (evidence: 5-6,8-9).

secondary_factors: The manager explained that production was off-season and the line was idle; the customer said an overview would suffice and later supplied footage (evidence: 7-8).
Price might change with a reduced integration scope, according to the customer’s discussion with the manager (evidence: 6).

what_could_be_done: After receiving the video, give the customer a dated production-review update and confirm the installation boundary, measurements, and revised price for the applicator-only scope.
limits: Compatibility depended on technical review of the customer’s existing conveyor; the retained view does not show that assessment or whether faster follow-up would change the result (evidence: 6,9).

evidence.paraphrase: Manager worklog records a flat 10-liter HDPE canister, two side labels, and target throughput; these baseline specifications are not independently repeated in the retained customer messages.
The customer sent a canister sketch and label examples with dimensions.
The manager acknowledged receipt and said the information had been passed to the technical department for equipment approval.
The manager presented the proposal and arranged a follow-up discussion; the customer tentatively agreed to try the proposed time.
The manager sent the commercial proposal and asked the customer to review it and provide feedback.
The customer confirmed receiving the proposal but said it had reviewed it only partly and planned to compare options before deciding how to proceed.

The customer said the offered machine included its own conveyor, whereas the customer needed to reuse its existing conveyor and add or replace applicators; the customer asked whether this could be done and how scope might affect price.

The customer acknowledged the requested video was not yet sent, said it would try the next day, and said an overview would suffice; the manager explained that production was off-season and the line was idle.
The customer sent production video footage.
The manager thanked the customer for the video and said it had been sent to production for review.

uncertainties: This audit is chronology-contaminated: during preprocessing I saw the removed terminal call at original source_line 33, activity_id 673329. Its content is not used in this retained-view assessment, but independent blind status cannot be claimed.
The baseline throughput and product details are manager-worklog claims; customer messages directly establish the existing-conveyor integration requirement and the supplied video.
The retained view ends while production review is pending; no technical response or final resolution is established here.
